reasons: The lake identity record gives case_name_full as Griffin v. Wisconsin, court as U.S. Supreme Court, date_decided as 1987-06-26, and year as 1987.
The lake citations record lists official citation 483 U.S. 868, parallel citations 107 S. Ct. 3164, 97 L. Ed. 2d 709, and 55 U.S.L.W. 5156, and vendor-neutral citation 1987 U.S. LEXIS 2897.
The opinion states that the search satisfied the Fourth Amendment because it was carried out pursuant to a regulation that itself satisfies the Fourth Amendment's reasonableness requirement.

The opinion states: "We think it clear that the special needs of Wisconsin’s probation system make the warrant requirement impracticable and justify replacement of the standard of probable cause by “reasonable grounds,” as defined by the Wisconsin Supreme Court."
The opinion later states that the search of Griffin's residence was reasonable because it was conducted pursuant to a valid regulation governing probationers.
residual_risks: The holding should not be read to approve any probationer home search on reasonable grounds outside the valid-regulation framework; the opinion expressly declined that broader question.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Tie the holding to a valid probation regulation governing probationers, as interpreted by the Wisconsin Supreme Court, rather than a free-standing reasonable-grounds rule.
